prompt: Bromine ($[\text{Ar}]3d^{10}4s^{2}4p^{5}$) is in which block, period and group?
markscheme: **D.** The last electron enters a p orbital; outer level $n=4$; seven valence electrons: group 17.

concept: Period number and outer energy level
prompt: State what the period number of an element tells you about its electron configuration.
markscheme: The number of the outermost occupied main energy level, e.g. period 3 elements have valence electrons in $n=3$ **(A1)**

prompt: Explain the trends in atomic radius **(a)** across period 3 and **(b)** down group 1.
markscheme:
**(a)** Decreases: nuclear charge increases while electrons are added to the same main level with similar shielding, so they are pulled closer **(R1)(A1)**

**(b)** Increases: each element has an extra occupied main energy level **(R1)**

prompt: Explain why reactivity increases down group 1 but decreases down group 17.
markscheme:
Group 1 react by losing an electron; down the group the outer electron is further from the nucleus and more shielded, so it is lost more easily **(R1)**

Group 17 react by gaining an electron; down the group the incoming electron is further from the nucleus and less strongly attracted **(R1)**, so electron gain is harder **(A1)**

prompt: Write equations for the reactions of **(a)** sodium oxide with water and **(b)** sulfur trioxide with water, and state the nature of aluminium oxide.
markscheme:
**(a)** Na₂O + H₂O → 2NaOH (basic) **(A1)**

**(b)** SO₃ + H₂O → H₂SO₄ (acidic) **(A1)**

Al₂O₃ is amphoteric — it reacts with both acids and bases **(A1)**

prompt: What is the oxidation state of manganese in KMnO₄?
Explain why the first ionisation energy of **(a)** aluminium is lower than that of magnesium, and **(b)** sulfur is lower than that of phosphorus.
markscheme:
**(a)** Al's outer electron is in a 3p orbital, which is higher in energy and more shielded than Mg's 3s **(R1)(A1)**

**(b)** In S the electron is removed from a doubly occupied 3p orbital, where electron–electron repulsion makes it easier to remove **(R1)(A1)**

prompt: State two characteristic properties of transition elements, and why zinc is not considered a transition element.
markscheme:
Any two: variable oxidation states, coloured compounds, catalytic activity, complex ion formation, magnetic properties **(A1)**

Zinc forms only Zn²⁺, which has a full $3d^{10}$ sublevel — it has no incomplete d sublevel **(R1)**

prompt: Explain why transition elements show variable oxidation states.
markscheme: The 4s and 3d sublevels are close in energy **(R1)**, so successive ionisation energies increase gradually and different numbers of electrons can be lost (or shared) without a large energy jump **(R1)**

prompt: Explain why an aqueous solution of [Cu(H₂O)₆]²⁺ appears blue.
markscheme:
The ligands split the 3d orbitals into two sets of different energy **(A1)**

An electron is promoted from the lower to the higher set by absorbing light of a particular frequency (orange/red) **(R1)**

The colour observed is the complementary colour of the light absorbed — blue **(R1)**
